Détente

/day-TAHNT/ - the stress falls on TAHNT · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Détente means an easing of hostility between rivals.

The drama club and the robotics team slid into a détente this fall: the auditorium is traded by semester now, and the prop-room lock finally came off.

Worked Example

The two grandmasters had needled each other in interviews for a decade. The détente arrived quietly at the Vienna open — a shared analysis session, then coffee — and though each still wants the other's title, the sniping in print has stopped.

Détente is the easing, not the embrace: hostility cools while the rivalry underneath survives. A truce merely pauses open conflict; reconciliation makes friends again. Détente lives between them — rivals lowering the temperature on purpose.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

thaw: A thaw is the informal picture for hostility easing — ice loosening between people or governments after a long freeze — and a thaw can simply arrive as moods soften. A détente is the deliberate version: rivals choosing, step by step, to lower the temperature while remaining rivals.

lull: A lull is any quiet stretch in a conflict — the shelling pauses, the argument rests — and it merely happens, promising nothing about what follows. A détente is chosen and worked at: both rivals deciding to ease the hostility itself rather than wait it out.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

escalation: hostility deliberately turned up

flare-up: the sudden return of open conflict

Where it sits · how far the quarrel has healed — truce → détente → reconciliation

truce vs. détente: A truce stops short of a détente — it only halts the firing while both sides keep their positions and their anger, but a détente cools the hostility itself, on purpose.

reconciliation vs. détente: Reconciliation goes further than détente — a détente's rivals still circle each other warily; reconciliation means the quarrel itself is over and both sides mean it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dé-

Prefix — dé-: un-, undoing (French, from Latin dis-)

Root — tente

Root — tente: stretched tight (from Latin tendere, to stretch)

Put it together

Put it together: Dé- (un-) + tente (stretched tight) = an un-tightening. French détente named the release of a crossbow's taut string before it ever named diplomacy. The picture does the work: two rivals have been winding the rope tighter for years, and détente is the first deliberate slackening — tension let out, not friendship tied on.

Use the root in a new word: tension

Use the root in a new word: tension: You could feel the tension leave the room when the results finally posted.

Root Check

Word Choice

diplomatic / journalistic

Détente is the Cold War's loanword for rivals easing off — governments, companies, feuding clubs — while staying rivals. A truce pauses open conflict; reconciliation ends it; détente just lowers the temperature. Keep the accent and the French sound, day-TAHNT. You may also meet detent, no accent — a machine part's catch — which is a different word.
